title: Abdominal X-ray
what: A simple X-ray of the belly, without contrast dye. It shows gas, fluid, and some stones.
why: For severe belly pain, bloating, no stool or gas passing, a possible bowel blockage, or a swallowed object.
duration: usually 5 to 10 minutes in the room; with sudden pain, the doctor looks at the image right away
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
If you recently had a barium test. Barium shows on the image
If an object was swallowed, say what and when

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: Usually none. In an emergency, the image is taken right away.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Take off jewelry and anything metal in the area. Sometimes you are asked to change.

bring: Past belly images and ultrasounds, if you have them
steps: You remove metal items and change, if asked
The image is taken standing or lying down, sometimes both
You hold your breath for a couple of seconds
The technician takes the image and checks that everything is visible
feel: It does not hurt. The image itself takes a fraction of a second
Sometimes you need to hold an awkward position for a bit
after: The doctor who sent you will decide what is next
The report is usually ready the same day, or right away if urgent
red_flags: Severe belly pain that keeps getting worse, vomiting, a hard belly, or no stool or gas: call emergency services

faq.q: Does a belly X-ray show all the organs?
faq.a: No. It mainly shows gas, fluid, and dense objects. Organs are seen in more detail on ultrasound or CT.

faq.q: Do I need to fast before the X-ray?
faq.a: Usually not for a plain X-ray. If unsure, check with the clinic.

reminders.text: Abdominal X-ray soon. Wear clothes with no metal, and bring your referral.
